title: Commitment and Consistency: Hobgoblins of the Mind
coreMove: Treat consistency as evidence to inspect, not a command to continue.
sourcePressure: The source supports prior choices, public stands, visible commitments, statements, identities, self-alignment pressure, and lock-in that can stabilize action or trap people in bad continuance.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not write this as simple perseverance advice; the danger is obedience to an earlier self-signal that no longer fits.

hook: Your past self can trap you
The first yes wants a second

exampleSpecs.audience: a new member who publicly called herself serious
exampleSpecs.stakes: buying costly equipment to match a declared identity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she hears members repeat her serious observer label and checks nights actually spent outside before ordering
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a star chart folded under a red flashlight

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant menu redesign after a chef's public promise
exampleSpecs.audience: a chef-owner who announced a no-fried-food direction
exampleSpecs.stakes: keeping a failing menu because reversing feels humiliating
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chef compares sales slips to the old interview quote and decides the quote is not a business plan
exampleSpecs.firstImage: grease pencil marks across a laminated menu proof

exampleSpecs.audience: an organizer who gathered signatures on one demand
exampleSpecs.stakes: refusing a better repair sequence because the petition named a different first step
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the organizer reads the signed demand aloud, then asks whether consistency with the petition or solving leaks should govern the next move
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a clipboard of signatures under a leaking hallway ceiling stain

exampleSpecs.audience: a producer attached to a promised crafting system
exampleSpecs.stakes: spending six months on a feature because early backers heard the promise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the producer places the old campaign promise beside playtest notes showing the feature harms the game loop
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sticky notes clustered around a paper prototype map

exampleSpecs.audience: a resident known by classmates as future surgeon
exampleSpecs.stakes: ranking a specialty for identity consistency rather than fit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the resident lists what the future surgeon label gives her and what the current rotation data says
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a call-room locker with wrinkled scrub caps on the shelf

exampleSpecs.audience: a donor chair who backed a costly steeple repair first
exampleSpecs.stakes: defending the first pledge while the roof worsens
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair says my first pledge was public, then moves the roof invoice beside it and names the current need
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cracked slate tile on a green felt meeting table

skillTargets: detect when a public stand is driving later behavior
choose language that updates a commitment without self-attack
evaluate whether identity alignment fits present evidence

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one old commitment on your calendar and say what present evidence, not pride, would justify keeping it.
